title: What remains is pious memory, praise, and imitation of faith, hope, and the other virtues
source_text: XXXV. At, inquies, quid ergo restat ex Doctorum Ecclesiae Reformatae sententia, quo Sanctos honorare & colere possimus? Respondeo, juxta ipsos, honorem illum consistere in pia & frequenti illorum commemoratione; in eo quod magnifice de ipsis sentiamus, laudes eorum, quum se fert occasio, celebremus, eorumque virtutes & egregia facta sedulo recolamus, & in animum revocemus. Praesertim vero in eo, quod eorum exemplum sequamur, doctrinam amplectamur, & spem, fidem, charitatem, zelum, fortitudinem, patientiam & humilitatem, qua nobis praeluxerunt, toto animi conatu aemulemur.
pass_a_gloss: But, you will say, what then remains, according to the opinion of the doctors of the Reformed Church, by which we can honor and cultivate the Saints? I answer, according to them, that that honor consists in a pious and frequent commemoration of them; in this, that we think magnificently of them, celebrate their praises when occasion offers, and diligently recollect their virtues and excellent deeds and call them back into the mind. But especially in this, that we follow their example, embrace their doctrine, and with the whole effort of the mind emulate the hope, faith, charity, zeal, fortitude, patience, and humility with which they have gone before us.
pass_b_english: Asked what honor of the Saints is left, Le Blanc answers from the Reformed doctors.
It is frequent pious remembrance, a high estimate, praise when there is occasion, and a careful recall of their virtues and great deeds.
Above all it is following their example, receiving their teaching, and striving to match their hope, faith, love, zeal, courage, patience, and humility.

lemmas.gloss: that we emulate with the whole effort of the mind

choices.why: Honor includes receiving what they taught, not only admiring their story.
